name: Microsoft Xbox 360 family
summary: Explore Xbox 360 hardware in its three body styles and many motherboard revisions. Homebrew eligibility is decided by both the board revision and the dashboard/kernel version: JTAG on old kernels, RGH on fat and slim boards (and 360 E Stingray boards with a postfix adapter, not Barracuda/Winchester), and Bad Update (software-only) on any model at dashboard 2.0.17559.

specs.cpu: IBM PowerPC triple-core (Xenon Waternoose on first boards; later revisions on smaller processes)
specs.storage: Detachable hard drive, model-dependent; memory units; USB storage on later dashboards
specs.media: DVD drive (HD-DVD via external add-on); no Blu-ray
specs.display: Up to 1080p; HDMI on Zephyr and later and on S/E models

variants.storage: 20 GB to 120 GB hard drive; 4 GB memory unit on some bundles
variants.notes: Board revisions named by free60: Xenon, Zephyr, Falcon (Opus), Jasper. The JTAG/SMC hack is patched at CB level on Jasper V4.1 and later (free60), so check the board before assuming JTAG. free60 documents the reset glitch hack for fat consoles.

specs.gpu: ATI Y1 (90 nm) with 10 MB eDRAM
specs.hdmi: Zephyr and later (free60: Zephyr was the first revision with HDMI)

variants.storage: 4 GB to 250 GB depending on SKU
variants.notes: Board revisions named by free60: Trinity (Valhalla), Corona. free60 documents the reset glitch hack for slim consoles and calls it unpatchable on slims. Peer Pressure works on Trinity only (ConsoleMods).

variants.storage: 250 GB or 4 GB/500 GB depending on SKU
variants.notes: Two board revisions: Stingray (Corona-like) and Barracuda (Winchester). ConsoleMods: Stingray boards can use RGH with a postfix adapter; Barracuda boards are not compatible with RGH at all. Bad Update is confirmed on Winchester consoles by its author.

firmware.version: 2.0.17559 (latest; Microsoft no longer ships new 360 dashboards)

homebrew.name: Bad Update
homebrew.summary: A hypervisor exploit for every 360 model running dashboard 2.0.17559. It enters through a supported game save (Rock Band Blitz; Tony Hawk's American Wasteland is deprecated) or an exploited Avatar and runs an unsigned default.xex, such as FreeMyXe. Non-persistent — power-off returns the console to stock.

compatibility.note: The exploit author states it works at dashboard 17559 and confirms Winchester consoles; free60 states any 360 model on 17559. Does not work on Xbox One or Series.

requirements: A supported game (Rock Band Blitz trial or full game) or an exploited Avatar, a FAT32 USB stick and an unsigned default.xex.
warnings: Non-persistent — code execution is lost at power-off.
Only works at dashboard 2.0.17559; a different dashboard does not have the exploit.

homebrew.name: FreeMyXe
homebrew.firmware: 2.0.17559 only, inside a Bad Update session
homebrew.summary: A lightweight patch set applied at runtime by Bad Update: it patches the kernel and hypervisor with xeBuild-derived patches, lets homebrew reach the hypervisor and CPU key, and can launch XeLL or an unsigned default.xex. Non-persistent.

compatibility.note: Runs after the Bad Update exploit at dashboard 2.0.17559; the README names XeUnshackle as the fuller alternative.

requirements: A Bad Update session on dashboard 2.0.17559 and the FreeMyXe payload on USB.
warnings: Non-persistent; power-off returns the console to stock.
The README warns not to flash a modified NAND or write to flash — that bricks the console.

homebrew.name: XeUnshackle
homebrew.firmware: 2.0.17559 only, inside a Bad Update session
homebrew.summary: A Bad Update payload that applies a full xeBuild-derived hypervisor and kernel patch set, loads DashLaunch's launch.xex, and displays or dumps the CPU key, DVD key and 1BL. Non-persistent.

compatibility.note: README: designed for Xbox360BadUpdate, which works on any 360 model at dashboard 2.0.17559, including Winchester.

requirements: A Bad Update session on dashboard 2.0.17559 and the XeUnshackle payload on USB.
warnings: Non-persistent; power-off returns the console to stock.
README: back up the NAND first and never flash a modified NAND or replace files in flash — that bricks the console.

homebrew.name: RGH family (Reset Glitch Hack)
homebrew.firmware: Dashboard-version limits per RGH variant not verified at a fetchable primary source
homebrew.summary: A permanent boot-time glitch mod: a reset pulse sent while the CPU is slowed makes the bootloader hash check pass so a custom bootloader runs. free60 documents the method for fat consoles (glitching CB) and slim consoles (glitching CB_A, unpatchable), and says the custom CD loads the base kernel from NAND, patches it and runs it. Requires a glitch chip (CPLD), NAND programmer and soldering. ConsoleMods covers the later variant names and the 360 E split: Stingray boards need a postfix adapter, Barracuda (Winchester) boards are not RGH-compatible.

compatibility.note: free60 documents the fat-console glitch (CB stage); ConsoleMods lists the later variants and their board limits.
free60 documents the slim-console glitch (CB_A stage, unpatchable). ConsoleMods: Trinity and Corona are supported; Waitsburg needs a postfix adapter.

requirements: A NAND dump (dumped twice and compared) before any work.
Glitch chip (CPLD), NAND programmer and soldering equipment.
warnings: A bad install can leave the console unbootable until the chip is removed and the NAND restored.
Soldering a glitch chip is not reversible by software.

homebrew.name: JTAG (SMC hack)
homebrew.firmware: 2.0.7371 or lower; some Jasper, Tonasket and refurbished Xenon units have a patched CB even on 7371 (ConsoleMods)
homebrew.summary: A permanent boot-time exploit that runs homebrew via an old (4532) kernel on phat consoles with an unpatched CB (free60). Patched at CB level on Jasper V4.1 and later; ConsoleMods puts the dashboard limit at 2.0.7371 or lower and warns that some Jasper, Tonasket and refurbished Xenon consoles were patched even on 7371.

compatibility.note: free60 lists Jasper V4.1 as patched on CB level. ConsoleMods: 2.0.7371 or lower, but some Jasper, Tonasket and refurbished Xenon units have a patched CB even on 7371. Dump the NAND and check the CB before assuming a console is JTAG-able.

requirements: An unpatched CB and a dashboard at 2.0.7371 or lower (ConsoleMods; free60: Jasper V4.1 and later are patched on CB level).
A NAND dump to verify the CB state.
warnings: A dashboard version alone does not prove JTAG — the CB must be unpatched.

homebrew.name: Peer Pressure
homebrew.summary: A software exploit for phat consoles and Trinity slims at dashboard 2.0.17559. Does not work on Corona, Waitsburg or 360 E boards.

compatibility.note: Only Trinity boards support Peer Pressure. Corona and Waitsburg do not.

requirements: Dashboard 2.0.17559 on a phat or a Trinity slim.
warnings: Only Trinity slims are listed as supported (ConsoleMods).

homebrew.name: Linux (free60 distributions)
homebrew.firmware: Requires a modded console with XeLL; no firmware-specific limit
homebrew.summary: An archive of Linux distributions from free60: Debian (etch through sid), Ubuntu 7.10 and 11.10, a LiveCD, and Gentoo (2025). Booting any of it needs a hacked console with XeLL; the older images are not maintained current distributions.

compatibility.note: Historical archive; booting requires XeLL and a modded console.

requirements: A modded Xbox 360 with XeLL installed.
warnings: Not a supported way to run Linux today. Kernels and distro images are historical.

homebrew.name: XeLL (Xenon Linux Loader)
homebrew.firmware: Loaded by a hack; no firmware version of its own
homebrew.summary: A second-stage bootloader run by a hack: it catches the CPU threads, loads an ELF file from CD or over TFTP, and launches it. It is made to boot Linux and carries a flat device tree, but can also load libXenon homebrew.

compatibility.note: free60: XeLL is booted by the SMC (JTAG) or reset glitch hack; neither page lists model or firmware limits for XeLL itself.
free60 Bad Update guide: FreeMyXe can launch XeLL Reloaded on a 360 at dashboard 2.0.17559; Bad Update is confirmed on Winchester.

requirements: A console with a working hack that can load XeLL (SMC/JTAG, RGH, or Bad Update with FreeMyXe).
warnings: XeLL is a loader, not an entry point; it does nothing on a stock console.

links.label: free60: Bad Update guide (launches XeLL Reloaded)

homebrew.name: Aurora
homebrew.firmware: Requires a hacked console; no firmware version of its own
homebrew.summary: A custom replacement dashboard built around a coverflow game launcher, with skins, cover and title-update downloads, categories, FTP and a plugin system. It launches as Aurora.xex, or as the default dashboard through DashLaunch.

compatibility.note: ConsoleMods documents the install on a hacked 360 and says to launch Aurora.xex or set it as the default dashboard with DashLaunch; it lists no model or firmware limits.

requirements: A hacked console that can run unsigned .xex files; DashLaunch is only needed to make Aurora the default dashboard.
warnings: Aurora is a dashboard, not an entry point; it needs an existing hack that runs unsigned code.

homebrew.name: Freestyle Dash (FSD)
homebrew.firmware: Requires a hacked console; no firmware version of its own
homebrew.summary: A customizable replacement dashboard by Team FSD that scans and categorizes Xbox 360, XBLA and original Xbox games, launches homebrew, downloads cover art and runs plugins. The last official release is FSD3 Rev 755; ConsoleMods links a patched build that fixes its stability issues.

compatibility.note: ConsoleMods documents FSD as a replacement dashboard and links the FSD3 release; it lists no model or firmware limits.

requirements: A hacked console that can run unsigned .xex files.
warnings: FSD is a dashboard, not an entry point; it needs an existing hack that runs unsigned code.

homebrew.name: XeXMenu
homebrew.firmware: Runs on a hacked console; no firmware version of its own
homebrew.summary: A dashboard and file manager for modified 360s, usually the first dashboard installed because its installer appears under My Games in the official dash. Version 1.2 only adds skins over 1.1, and it is less featured than Aurora or Freestyle Dash.

compatibility.note: ConsoleMods: XeXMenu is a dashboard for JTAG/RGH consoles; the page lists no model or firmware limits.
FreeMyXe README: Bad Update can launch homebrew such as XeXMenu; Bad Update works on any 360 model at 2.0.17559, including Winchester.

requirements: A hacked console that can run unsigned .xex files.
warnings: XeXMenu is a dashboard, not an entry point; it needs an existing hack that runs unsigned code.

homebrew.name: J-Runner with Extras
homebrew.firmware: Reads and writes the NAND; not a firmware version
homebrew.summary: Windows application for RGH/JTAG work, described by its project as "The Ultimate RGH/JTAG App": NAND reading and writing, glitch-chip programming and image building. It is a desktop tool, not a route into the console by itself.

compatibility.note: Desktop tool for RGH/JTAG consoles; it does not add an entry point of its own.

requirements: An x86 Windows PC (Vista SP2 or later) with .NET Framework 4.5.2, a USB 2.0 port for the hardware device, and a NAND programmer or flasher supported by the tool.
warnings: NAND writes are destructive; keep verified backups and never flash an image you did not build for this console.

homebrew.name: Xbox 360 system software update and reinstall
homebrew.summary: Official update and recovery for Xbox 360. The final dashboard is 2.0.17559; reinstalling does not accept older firmware.

compatibility.note: Official update track shared by the whole family.

requirements: USB drive with the official update file.

officialSupport.summary: Microsoft no longer ships new dashboards; the 2024-07-29 Store closure ended purchases, not system updates.
